column3: NASB renders “servant” as “bond-servant” and “a called apostle” as “called as an apostle.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “having come of the seed of David” as “born of a descendant of David.”
NASB reorders the verse, placing “by the resurrection from the dead” before “according to the Spirit of holiness”; “in power” is rendered “with power.”
NASB renders “unto obedience of faith” as “to bring about the obedience of faith” and “on behalf of His name” as “for His name's sake.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “called saints” as “called as saints” and reorders the verse. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text (“for”).
NASB adds “the preaching of” and “as to,” and moves “is my witness” after the relative clause.
NASB renders “imploring” as “making request” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “to the strengthening of you” as “that you may be established.”
NASB adds “while among you” and “each of us.”
NASB renders “purposed” as “planned” and puts “and have been prevented thus far” in parentheses.
NASB renders “a debtor I am” as “I am under obligation.”
NASB renders “readiness” as “I am eager.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of Christ”; it adds “also.”
The quotation is in capitals, with the supplied word “man.”
NASB renders “upon” as “against” and “suppressing” as “who suppress.”
NASB renders “manifest” as “evident” and “has revealed” as “made it evident.”
NASB renders “invisible qualities” as “invisible attributes” and “divinity” as “divine nature,” and it reorders the verse.
NASB adds “even though,” and renders “glorified” as “honor” and “thinking” as “speculations.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “changed … into” as “exchanged … for,” “immortal” and “mortal” as “incorruptible” and “corruptible,” and “likeness of an image” as “image in the form of.”
NASB follows the critical text without “also”; “desires” is rendered “lusts.”
NASB renders “changed” as “exchanged,” “the falsehood” as “a lie,” “beyond” as “rather than,” and “to the ages” as “forever.”
NASB renders “passions of dishonor” as “degrading passions” and “use” as “function.”
NASB renders “use” as “function,” “the shame” as “indecent acts,” and “recompense” as “due penalty.”
NASB renders “to have in knowledge” as “to acknowledge” and adds “any longer.”
NASB follows the critical text without “sexual immorality”; “covetousness” is rendered “greed,” and “malice” is “evil.” It adds “they are.”
NASB renders “hateful to God” as “haters of God.”
